notes: Known implementation mismatch: specified-side swaps revert with UnrepresentableFee if the request exceeds uint128 or the full-fill reservation or expected pool amount exceeds int128, even when a price-limited partial fill would fit. This is stricter than the brief's int256-only overflow exception. Reservation rounding also permits up to two IMD minor units of fee dust above the floored rate on the actual fill. SNEWTHook(IPoolManager manager, address launchToken) takes $poolManager then $token, with no owner, factory or treasury argument. $poolManager resolves to the chain's Uniswap v4 PoolManager (0x8366a39cc670b4001a1121b8f6a443a643e40951 on Robinhood Chain); $token resolves to the SNEWT deployed by the factory. The constructor makes no external call. Treasury 0x5f948c351eb9f0734c28b605bbeee9ab9d04318e is a compile-time constant. Deploy SNEWTHook directly using a CREATE2 salt mined for beforeInitialize (1<<13), beforeSwap (1<<7), afterSwap (1<<6), beforeSwapReturnDelta (1<<3) and afterSwapReturnDelta (1<<2): (uint160(hook) & 0x3fff) == 0x20cc. The constructor validates those permissions. Enabled callbacks accept calls only from the PoolManager. beforeInitialize accepts one pool containing SNEWT at static LP fee 12500 and tick spacing 60, records the paired currency and openedAt, and does not authenticate the initializer or pin IMD. The factory must deploy and initialize atomically with the manifest's IMD pair to prevent another pair binding first. pool.initialPrice is the required one-to-one sqrtPriceX96 provenance value; the factory derives the actual opening price from launch economics and token ordering. The pool's static 1.25% LP fee is never made dynamic or overridden. The additional hook fee is denominated in IMD: 4000 bps at initialization, declining with block.timestamp as 4000 - floor(3700 * elapsedSeconds / 3600) during the first 60 minutes, then 300 bps forever. These fee parameters are constants. When IMD is unspecified, afterSwap charges against the real BalanceDelta; when IMD is specified, beforeSwap reserves for a full fill and afterSwap scales the reservation to the actual fill. Excess reservation becomes an ERC-6909 IMD claim for the nonzero address supplied as canonical 32-byte abi.encode(refundRecipient) in hookData. Empty, zero or malformed data falls back to the PoolManager caller, usually the router; a router without claim forwarding must supply the swapper's recipient explicitly. Liquidity exhaustion can cause partial fills even at full price limits. Exact-output sells whose fill is below the reservation still require IMD settlement funded by the seller or an authorized claim-burning flow; an explicit refund recipient alone does not remove that requirement, and TAKE_ALL-only settlement cannot handle a negative output delta. The fee bound includes the refund claim, which can be transferred or redeemed separately. Fees accrue as the hook's ERC-6909 IMD claims on the PoolManager. Anyone may call sweep() to redeem all pending claims to the fixed treasury; an empty sweep reverts with NothingToSweep. Views: feeNow(), openedAt(), pending(), collected(), swept(). No owner, setters, proxy, upgradeability, delegatecall or selfdestruct. Supply and allocation are governed by the separate launch policy, not this manifest.
